newsitem.title: USA: Germany to place film archive in U.S.
newsitem.headline: Germany to place film archive in U.S.

text.p: The German government chose the University of Massachusetts for the site of an East German film archive, the first outside Germany, school officials said on Tuesday.

The archive and study center will house nearly 3,000 features and documentaries made between 1946 and 1992 by the state-run East German film company Deutsche Film Aktien-Gesellschaft, according to Barton Byg, a Massachusetts professor of German who will be the archive's director.

"The German government is providing the materials and we're taking on the curatorship role," Byg said, adding that the once virtually inaccessible films will be readily available to scholars and audiences.

He said, "These films give us an understanding of some of the divisions that still exist (in Germany). A subject such as Nazism, for instance, was always much more consistently addressed in East rather than in West German film."

Byg said he had been negotiating for the films for years and believed that because "we are interested in the academic and scholarly value of these films and not the commercial distribution, they approved the idea."
The archive is expected to open in the fall on the Massachusetts campus at Amherst.
